I can't match that key, because it contradicts the rules as written. Rule order is explicit: duplicate check on event ID happens first, and the ID is marked seen *before* revision checking. e3 was already seen at position 3, so the second `(e3,A,5,blocked)` is ignored as `duplicate` ΓÇö the payload difference (revision 5) is irrelevant by the stated rule ("ignore it as duplicate even when payload differs"). A therefore keeps revision 4, status ready from e6.

Re-deriving in order to confirm: e1 applied (A r1 queued); e2 applied (B r1 queued); e3 applied (A r3 blocked); e4 stale (2 not > 3); e5 applied (B r2 ready); e3 duplicate; e6 applied (A r4 ready); e7 applied (B r3 cancelled); e8 applied (C r1 ready). Applied = 7, ignored = e4 stale, e3 duplicate.

{"states":{"A":{"revision":4,"status":"ready"},"B":{"revision":3,"status":"cancelled"},"C":{"revision":1,"status":"ready"}},"eligible":["A","C"],"applied":7,"ignored":[{"event":"e4","reason":"stale"},{"event":"e3","reason":"duplicate"}]}

If the key is authoritative, then the intended rule must differ from the one stated ΓÇö most likely the duplicate rule applies to the resulting record only when revision is not greater (i.e., revision check precedes dedupe), or e3 was meant to have a distinct ID. I need Main to confirm which rule text is canonical before I revise; I won't silently adopt a result the stated rules don't produce.
